transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~36 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (CTO), Jenna (Product), Sam (SRE)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on Redwood PLG quickstart, free credits and time-to-first-token for a small internal pilot. Customer wants to understand hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for latency, cost, and data residency. Security topics (SOC2, KMS, SSO) surfaced; SE to run a short benchmark and share runbook.

Topics:
- Quickstart path and SDKs
- Free credits and onboarding timeline
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for their telemetry workload
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and KV cache
- Security: SSO, audit logs, KMS, SOC2
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is alex from redwood, i'll hand to priya to do a quick tech intro, but first quick round robin?
[00:18] Mark: yeah hi mark here, cto at northstar, we run real-time analytics for shipping telematics, interested in LLM for summarization alerts and support automation.
[00:28] Jenna: jenna product, trying to move fast - want to see time to value and easy sdk.
[00:35] Sam: sam, infra, i'm worried about latency and data retention constraints, we have pii in telemetry.
[00:43] Priya: awesome, thanks. quick context on quickstart: there's a self-serve api, free credits for trial, and our quickstart repo gets you first token in minutes. we'll show typical flow: api key, sample curl, python/js sdk, and a simple embed/generation example.
[01:05] Alex: quick note, many customers start hosted because it's fastest to get going; then we discuss Dedicated if they need predictable throughput or Private for strict residency.
[01:18] Mark: can you clarify hosted vs dedicated? specifically for throughput: if we send spikes of events, will hosted auto-scale?
[01:29] Priya: yes hosted auto-scales but there's cold start variability; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and consistent latency, plus options for burst capacity. for buffering/spikes we recommend queueing + batching and we have autoscale policies.
[01:47] Sam: and private? we have SOC2 and data residency asks, possibly on-prem in EU for some customers.
[01:55] Priya: Private gives you a VPC/on-prem option with a customer-managed control plane and integrations to your KMS/HSM. we also provide audit logs and RBAC. some perf tradeoffs but it meets compliance.
[02:12] Jenna: how long to get the quickstart working? we have a 2 week pilot goal.
[02:18] Alex: Typical time-to-first-token is under 15 minutes for devs; end-to-end pilot in 1-2 weeks if you run our quickstart and a few benchmark prompts. we'll give you free credits to cover initial testing.
[02:30] Mark: ok that helps. what about cost per token and options to reduce costs? quantization? batching?
[02:36] Priya: right - cost levers: batching, prefix/KV cache, quantized model variants; Redwood Optimize suggests model/quantization choices by workload. for streaming telemetry summarization you can moderate max tokens and enable caching for repeated context.
[02:55] Sam: you mentioned KV cash earlier, is that persistent across requests? (laughs)
[02:59] Priya: kv cash yes, sorry kv cache - it's a cache for key value attention states to speed up repeated prefix work, reduces token compute.
[03:12] Mark: any support for open models like Llama-family or others? vendor lock concerns.
[03:18] Alex: we host curated open models and also support customer models in Private. we avoid vendor lock by allowing you to pin versions and route to compatible variants; customers often compare us to OpenAI and Anthropic primarily for hosted APIs.
[03:33] Jenna: do you provide SDKs and example microservices?
[03:36] Priya: yes python/js/ts SDKs, example serverless wrappers, and a quickstart repo with a sample pipeline. we'll share links.
[03:43] Mark: security - how do you handle keys and encryption in hosted?
[03:47] Alex: hosted keys are managed by Redwood by default, but we have KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private. data in transit encrypted, at rest encrypted; audit logs available. SOC2 report available on request.
[04:02] Sam: ok timeline for SOC2 docs? we need to review for procurement.
[04:08] Alex: i'll include SOC2, ISO notes and our security FAQ; we can set up a separate security review call if needed.
[04:16] Mark: for the pilot, can we do a small batch of 1000 daily requests and then scale?
[04:22] Priya: absolutely. for that load hosted is usually fine; if you need <50ms p99 then Dedicated is recommended.
[04:33] Jenna: what's typical p99 on hosted?
[04:36] Priya: depends on model and sequence length; for short summarization with curated small models you can see 50-120ms p50 and 200-400ms p99 in hosted. Dedicated often halves that for same configuration.
[04:53] Mark: interesting. we will run some real prompts. can you help with benchmarking?
[04:58] Priya: yes i'll run a short benchmark runbook; we'll ask you to share 10 representative prompts and a seq length distribution.
[05:08] Sam: we use GKE and have internal service accounts - any specific networking steps to connect?
[05:14] Priya: quickstart has examples for env vars and secrets; for Private/VPC we do peering or private endpoints. we'll note the exact steps in the runbook.
[05:24] Alex: any procurement blockers? are you able to use hosted initially?
[05:28] Mark: procurement needs SOC2 + SSO. we prefer SAML SSO for company accounts.
[05:34] Alex: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning on enterprise tiers and for Dedicated/Private you can enforce SSO.
[05:42] Jenna: will the free credits show in the console? how do devs get them?
[05:46] Alex: yes we provision credits to the account email; quickstart includes a redemption link. devs can spin up tokens and try curl or sdk.
[05:55] Mark: any one-click demo or sandbox?
[05:57] Priya: quickstart is like a sandbox template, and we have hosted examples in the console that let you run playground prompts with sample data.
[06:07] Sam: about logging - does Redwood send full request logs back to our account or to redwood only? we need to control PII flow.
[06:14] Alex: by default hosted request logs are available in your console with redaction options; for strict PII you can opt out and use Private so logs stay on-prem. we'll document retention windows.
[06:25] Mark: okay good. are there any limitations on model size for Private?
[06:29] Priya: depends on the on-prem hardware and licensing, but we support large models; we can advise on quantization/serving profiles.
[06:36] Jenna: can we demo a quick end-to-end? even just an SDK example?
[06:39] Priya: sure i'll share code snippets here in chat after the call and attach quickstart link.
[06:45] Alex: for next steps, we propose: priya shares quickstart + runbook + bench steps; alex sends pricing and Dedicated one-pager; mark to confirm pilot prompts by next tuesday.
[06:59] Mark: sounds good, can you also include any recommended small-model suggestions for cost?
[07:03] Priya: yes we'll propose a small-curated set and quantization options.
[07:08] Jenna: timeline: try quickstart this week, pilot run next week, decision by end of month.
[07:14] Sam: i may need a short topology doc for infra team.
[07:17] Alex: we'll include a network/connectivity checklist.
[07:21] Mark: perfect thanks all.
[07:23] Alex: thanks everyone we'll follow up with materials.

Recap & Next Steps:
- Priya to send quickstart repo, runbook, and benchmark instructions (free credits instructions included).
- Alex to send pricing sheet and Dedicated one-pager + SOC2 docs.
- Mark to share 10 sample prompts and expected seq length distribution by 2026-06-22.
- Schedule security deep dive if procurement requests detailed review.

Links referenced (to be shared):
